# Darkroom's invariants

The promises Darkroom keeps, numbered, each with the test or Semgrep rule that holds it. The second review (fleet's `agent-review.yml`, on a pull request labelled `safety-critical` or `security` or changing a path `.github/workflows/agent-review.yml` lists) checks every one a change touches: it still holds, the named check still holds it, and the change carries a positive and a negative test for it. Items 1 to 6 are `AGENTS.md`'s "Darkroom's promises"; a check named with an issue number is added by that issue, before the code it guards. The sections after them belong to the safety-critical issues, each filled in by its own pull request and never rewritten afterwards: a later change appends.

1. **An original is written once.** Nothing under a person's `originals/` is modified, moved or deleted by the service. Held by Semgrep's `darkroom-originals-read-only` and a before/after listing test (#25).
2. **Dedupe deletes nothing on Unraid.** It decides and records. Cleanup removes only staging, archives and resolved review holds, 14 days after the fact. Held by `tests/test_cleanup.py` and the dedupe invariants (#24, #26).
3. **A photo is eligible for deletion from an iPhone only when** every resource of it (photo, Live Photo video, adjusted version) is on Unraid with a verified SHA-1 and matched in a Takeout export by an unreversed automatic tier 1 or 2 decision, from a Google account that serves its owner, re-checked right before deleting. Held by Semgrep's `darkroom-eligibility-single-path` and `tests/test_eligibility_invariants.py` (#37).
4. **The browser worker never types a Google password or 2FA code.** A person signs in. Held by `tests/browser/test_no_credentials.py` (#28).
5. **Metadata gaps are filled with XMP sidecars, never by rewriting media.** Held by Semgrep's `darkroom-xmp-only-sidecars` (#25).
6. **No design changes without the owner's sign-off.** No web UI or iPhone screen merges unless it matches the design the owner signed off in `docs/design/` (#16, #34); a UI pull request carries screenshots. Held by review.

## Dedupe invariants (#24)

Filled in by #24's pull request: its invariants 1 to 6, each naming the test or Semgrep rule that holds it.

1. **The candidate set is exactly `accounts.served_people(account)`.** `PersonIndex.load(opened, account_id)` computes the served people itself (a caller cannot pass a wider set) and loads their phone items plus the Takeout items placed from this account's own exports; `decide` ignores any item outside `person_ids` even in a hand-built index; `apply` refuses a decision whose matched item or assigned person is outside the served set, or whose matched Takeout item came from another account's export. An identical file owned by a person the account doesn't serve becomes Google-only for the default person. Held by `tests/test_dedupe_invariants.py` (`CandidateSetIsTheServedPeople`) and `tests/test_dedupe.py` (`SharedPixelTests`, `OverlappingAccountsTests`, `PureIndexTests`).
2. **Nothing is deleted, moved or written by `darkroom/domain/dedupe.py`; it only decides and records.** It imports no file or process module, calls no delete, and leaves the folder tree and every `MediaItem` row in place. Held by `tests/test_dedupe_invariants.py` (`NothingIsDeletedMovedOrWritten`: a before/after hash of a tree with originals, google-only, review and staging files, and an AST check of the module).
3. **Only an automatic tier 1 or tier 2 decision matching a phone item sets `confirmed_in_google=True`, and only `darkroom/domain/dedupe.py` writes the flag.** Tiers 3, 4 and 5, owner-made decisions (#10 item 9 default), a tier 1 match on a placed Takeout item and an ambiguous tier 2 never set it. Held by `tests/test_dedupe_invariants.py` (`OnlyAutomaticTierOneAndTwoSetTheFlag`) and Semgrep's `darkroom-confirmed-flag-single-writer` (examples in `.semgrep/examples/darkroom/domain/confirmed_flag.py`).
4. **Every decision stores the export, the account, the tier, a reason, who decided and when; reversal sets `reversed_at` and clears the flag unless another unreversed automatic tier 1 or 2 decision still matches the same item.** Reversing twice keeps the first time; re-applying a reversed decision does not confirm again. Held by `tests/test_dedupe_invariants.py` (`DecisionsAreRecordedAndReversible`) and the property test `FlagImpliesAnUnreversedAutomaticMatch` (random households: a flag always has an unreversed automatic tier 1 or 2 decision from an account serving the item's owner).
5. **Applying the same item twice yields one decision.** A decision is keyed by export and the item's path in the export (`uq_dedupe_decisions_export_source`, migration 0004); a second apply returns the first row unchanged and adds no second `ReviewItem`. Held by `tests/test_dedupe_invariants.py` (`ApplyingTwiceYieldsOneDecision`) and `tests/test_migrations.py` (`test_0004_…`).
6. **Tier 2 matches only when exactly one candidate qualifies.** Sub-second capture time separates frames when both sides have it; two or more phone candidates, or another Takeout item of the same export qualifying for the same phone item, go to tier 4 review and never set the flag; an edited copy is never tier 2. Held by `tests/test_dedupe_invariants.py` (`TierTwoNeedsExactlyOneCandidate`) and `tests/test_dedupe.py` (`TierTwoAmbiguityTests`).

## Review actions (#27)

Filled in by #27's pull request: a review action never sets `confirmed_in_google`, with the test that holds it.

1. **Resolve, undo and reassign never set `confirmed_in_google`; reverse clears it unless another unreversed automatic tier 1 or 2 decision confirms the item.** `darkroom/domain/review.py` reaches the flag only through `dedupe.reverse` (with `by="owner"`); keep both places the held copy through `place.place_google_only`, which never touches the flag; skip writes nothing, and undo and reassign change no flag. Reversing a decision already reversed, or one whose pair is still pending in the queue, is refused with a 409 and changes nothing. Held by Semgrep's `darkroom-confirmed-flag-single-writer` and `tests/test_review_api.py` (`ResolveTests`, `UndoTests` and `DecisionTests`, comparing every item's flag before and after each action; `test_reversing_a_tier_one_match_clears_the_flag` also checks the original counts as unmatched again, and `test_reversing_keeps_the_flag_while_another_tier_one_or_two_decision_confirms`), and `tests/test_reassign.py` (`test_reassigning_moves_the_file_and_its_sidecar_and_rescans_both_libraries`).
2. **The hold stays until cleanup, and undo never outlives it.** Keep both is the only resolution: it sets `resolved_at`, the held copy stays in `_inbox/<person>/review/`, and `cleanup.clean_holds` removes it only 14 days after resolution (unchanged). Skip saves nothing: it only moves the page on to the next pair, so the pair stays pending and its hold is never scheduled for removal (`resolve` refuses any action but `keep_both`; `test_skip_is_not_a_server_action_and_changes_nothing`). A keep both that fails after its copy removes the copy and any sidecar it created and answers 409 (`test_keep_both_that_fails_after_copying_leaves_nothing_behind`). Undo is allowed only while `now - resolved_at < 14 days`, the hold is still there and the pair's decision is not reversed (a reversed pair never goes back to the queue, where it could not be decided), and returns the pair to `pending`, which cleanup never removes. Held by `tests/test_review_api.py` (`test_undo_is_allowed_inside_the_window_and_refused_after`, `test_a_reversed_pair_cannot_go_back_to_the_queue`, `test_cleanup_removes_the_hold_only_after_the_window_so_undo_and_cleanup_never_overlap`, `test_undo_without_the_hold_is_refused`) and `tests/test_cleanup.py`.
3. **Nothing leaves a google-only folder unless an identical copy stays.** Undoing keep both and reassigning remove a google-only file (and its `.xmp`) only through `paths.drop_library_copy`, which refuses any path outside `<person>/google-only/`, links, and a kept copy that is missing, outside the photo root, the same file or not byte-identical (SHA-1), and removes the file and its sidecar by first renaming both to a `.dropping-` name in the same folder, restoring both if either rename fails, so a failure never leaves one without the other; a `.dropping-` file whose final delete failed is swept from google-only folders by the cleanup pass (`paths.sweep_dropping`, only regular files inside a person's `google-only/`, an hour after the rename, and only while a byte-identical copy still exists in a library row's file or in the hold of a pair that is still pending, which cleanup never removes; a resolved pair's hold does not count, since cleanup deletes it 14 days later; a `.dropping-` sidecar goes only once its photo's `.dropping-` file is gone or goes in the same pass) (`tests/test_cleanup.py`, `InterruptedRemovalTests`). Undo leaves a kept copy another decision placed and refuses one an unreversed later decision matched. Reassign carries the existing `.xmp` byte for byte (writing one from the Takeout JSON only when there is none; any sidecar already at the target that is not byte-identical stops the move and is never changed), and if anything fails after its copy it removes only the copy and the sidecar it created, so a failed reassign changes no file; it sets the old copy and its sidecar aside (renamed) before the database commit and deletes them only after the commit succeeds, and if the commit fails it renames them back and removes the new copy; it refuses a photo a later import matched, a phone original, a file outside its person's google-only folder and a person who already has the photo. Held by `tests/test_paths.py` (`DropLibraryCopyTests`), `tests/test_review_api.py` (`UndoTests`) and `tests/test_reassign.py`.
4. **Reassign goes only to someone the export's account serves.** The target must be in `accounts.served_people` of the item's export account (single person: only that person, a no-op; shared Pixel: any served person); otherwise 409 and nothing changes. Reassign changes no account's served set, so `accounts.require_confirmations_kept` (#17) is untouched. Held by `tests/test_reassign.py` (`SharedAccountTests`, `SinglePersonAccountTests`).
5. **Thumbnails read only files under the photo root.** A library side is read through `Photos.original` (phone) or `Photos.inside` (takeout) and must be inside its person's folder; a held side through `cleanup.hold_file`; links and paths outside answer 404. Thumbnails are written only under `_inbox/<person>/.thumbs` with `paths.write_once`. Held by `tests/test_thumbs.py`.

## Placing and sidecars (#25)

Filled in by #25's pull request: how placing Takeout items and writing sidecars keeps promises 1 and 5, each naming the test or Semgrep rule that holds it.

1. **Placing never changes an original.** After a run over a fixture export (pair, read metadata, dedupe, place) every file that was under `originals/` before has the same SHA-1 after, and the only files added there are `<name>.<ext>.xmp` sidecars next to originals matched at tier 1 or 2. A second run changes no file anywhere under the photo folder. Held by `tests/test_place.py` (`FixtureExportRun`) and Semgrep's `darkroom-originals-read-only` (no `open(…, "w")`, `os.remove`, `os.rename`, `os.replace`, `shutil.move`/`copy*`, `rmtree` or `Path` write, unlink, rename or replace on a path from `Photos.originals`, `Photos.original`, `Photos.uploads_tmp` or a row's `originals_path` outside `darkroom/storage/paths.py`; examples in `.semgrep/examples/darkroom/domain/originals.py`).
2. **Every file is written through `darkroom/storage/paths.py`.** A placed or held item is copied with `paths.write_once` (exclusive create, never overwriting); a sidecar goes through `paths.write_sidecar`, which renders into a temporary folder beside it and then links or replaces only a target ending in `.xmp` that is a regular file or absent (a symlink or folder there is refused). Held by `tests/test_place.py` (`CollisionTests`) and `tests/test_xmp.py` (`WriteSidecarTests`, `FillTests.test_a_symlink_where_the_sidecar_goes_is_refused`).
3. **exiftool writes only sidecars.** `providers/exiftool.write_xmp` refuses any target not ending in `.xmp` and any tag outside `XMP-…`, writes with `-o` into a new file (never `-overwrite_original`), and merges an existing sidecar instead of clobbering it. Held by Semgrep's `darkroom-xmp-only-sidecars` (examples in `.semgrep/examples/darkroom/providers/exiftool.py`) and `tests/test_xmp.py` (`WriteXmpTests`).
4. **A sidecar fills only gaps.** It carries `XMP-exif:GPSLatitude`/`GPSLongitude` (the reference in the sign), `XMP-photoshop:DateCreated` with an offset and `XMP-dc:Description`, each only when the file's own metadata and the existing sidecar both lack it; a phone original gets location and description only. Nothing to add writes nothing. Held by `tests/test_xmp.py` (`GapsTests`, `FillTests`) and `tests/test_place.py` (`OriginalSidecarTests`).
5. **Only an unreversed automatic tier 1 or 2 match to a phone item adds a sidecar next to an original.** An owner-made decision, a reversed one, tier 3, a match to a placed Takeout item, a missing original or a stored path outside the owner's `originals/` adds nothing. Held by `tests/test_place.py` (`OriginalSidecarTests`).
6. **Google-only items go to the account's default person.** Whoever the decision or the Takeout JSON names, a tier 5 item is copied to the default person's `google-only/YYYY/MM/` (local capture date, else UTC date, else `undated/`) and its `MediaItem` saved there with its final path; a tier 4 item is copied to `_inbox/<person>/review/export-<id>/` and its `ReviewItem.hold_path` set. Staging is left for cleanup. Held by `tests/test_place.py` (`GoogleOnlyFolderTests`, `ReviewHoldTests`, `FixtureExportRun`).

## People, accounts and Pixels (#17)

Filled in by #17's pull request: editing who a Google account serves keeps dedupe invariant 4 and promise 3, each naming its test.

1. **An account keeps serving everyone it has confirmed photos for.** Changing a Pixel's people, moving a Pixel to another account, deleting a Pixel or changing an account's default person is refused with a 409 while the account it would stop serving someone through has an unreversed automatic tier 1 or 2 decision matching a phone item of that person, so a `confirmed_in_google` flag is never left backed only by an account that no longer serves the photo's owner. The check (`accounts.require_confirmations_kept`) runs before anything is written, so a refusal changes no row; nothing outside `darkroom/domain/dedupe.py` writes the flag. A change that keeps the owner served another way (another Pixel, the default person), a rename, adding people, and a reversed, owner-made or review decision do not hold it. Held by `tests/test_served_people_guard.py` (through the API, each with and without confirming decisions, comparing every table before and after a refusal) and the property test `FlagImpliesAnUnreversedAutomaticMatch` in `tests/test_dedupe_invariants.py`, which now changes Pixels and default people at random between applies and checks the flags after each change.
2. **Status never shows a count nothing has computed.** `/api/status` returns `null` for a person's unmatched originals and a device's photos safe to delete until #26 and #37 compute them, and the Status page shows "Not checked yet" for them, never a 0. Held by `tests/test_status_api.py` and `frontend/src/pages/Status.svelte.test.ts`.
3. **A new person never reuses a folder name that is on disk.** `people.create` refuses with a 409 when `<slug>/` or `_inbox/<slug>/` exists, because folders outlive a deleted person and indexing them would make the old person's originals the new person's photos, which feeds eligibility (promise 3). Held by `tests/test_people_api.py::test_a_deleted_persons_folder_name_is_never_reused_and_its_files_are_not_indexed`. If creating the folders fails part-way, the rollback lives in `Photos.ensure_person_tree` (`darkroom/storage/paths.py`, the one module allowed to touch these paths): it `rmdir`s only the directories that call made, deepest first and only if empty, never anything that existed or holds a file; no domain code removes a path under `originals/`. Held by `tests/test_paths.py::FailedTreeTests`.
4. **Deleting a Google account retires everything keyed by its id.** `accounts.delete` removes `_browser/<id>` (the Chromium profile and failure captures) through `Photos.retire_browser_account`, which refuses links and any path but that exact folder and fails the whole delete if the folder cannot go, and it closes the account's open alerts in the same transaction, because SQLite can reuse the id and a new account would otherwise inherit the old account's signed-in Google session. Held by `tests/test_pixels_api.py::AccountsApiTests`.

## Import run and cleanup (#26)

Filled in by #26's pull request: how the import orchestrator, the unmatched-originals alert and cleanup keep promises 1, 2 and 3, each naming the test or Semgrep rule that holds it.

1. **The import never sets `confirmed_in_google` itself.** `darkroom/domain/ingest/run.py` reaches the flag only through `dedupe.apply`; tiers 3, 4 and 5 and unmatched phone originals stay unconfirmed. Held by Semgrep's `darkroom-confirmed-flag-single-writer` and `tests/test_import_run.py` (`EndToEndTests.test_only_tier_one_and_two_phone_matches_are_confirmed`) and `tests/test_unmatched.py` (`SharedPixelTests.test_their_originals_stay_unconfirmed`).
2. **A run killed at or inside any stage, then restarted, ends in the same state as a run that was never killed.** The stage is committed on the export and the run after each stage (`unpacked`, `deduped`, `placed`, `counted`, `rescanned`, `reported`, `done`), decisions are committed one by one and keyed by export and path (#24's invariant 5), placing commits after each item and finds what an earlier attempt copied by hash; the files, decisions, items, review holds, counts, alerts, Immich scans and the single summary alert all match. Held by `tests/test_import_run.py` (`CrashTests`, comparing the whole state with a clean run's) and `EndToEndTests.test_importing_again_is_refused_and_changes_nothing`.
3. **One import at a time per account.** An exclusive `flock` on `<data>/locks/import-account-<id>.lock` (released by the kernel when a process dies) plus an in-process lock; a second import of the same account, from the scheduler, the API's queue or `run.py import-takeout`, is refused as busy and changes nothing. Held by `tests/test_import_run.py` (`OneAtATimeTests`, `QueueTests.test_the_scheduler_skips_an_account_that_is_busy`) and `tests/test_cli_import.py` (`test_an_import_already_running_for_the_account_is_refused`).
4. **A failed item never stops the run, and a failed run never claims success.** A per-item failure (metadata, decision, placing) becomes an `import_item_failed` event naming only the stage and the error type, is counted in `ImportRun.failed` and the summary; a stage failure marks the export and run `failed`, records `import_failed` and opens a failure alert, sends no summary and rescans nothing; a retry resumes at the recorded stage. Held by `tests/test_import_run.py` (`FailureTests`).
5. **The unmatched-originals alert only reports.** It counts a served person's phone originals indexed at least 7 days before the export was ready and not confirmed, per Pixel of the account serving them (the person alone when none does), opens when the count is above zero and closes when a later import brings it to zero; it writes no flag, changes no `PhoneAsset`, touches no file and its wording never mentions deleting. A newly opened alert's row is committed, marked sent, before it is sent, so a run killed after sending does not send it again. Held by `tests/test_unmatched.py` (`SharedPixelTests`, `SinglePersonTests`), `tests/test_alerts.py` (`test_wording`) and `tests/test_import_run.py` (`CrashTests.test_killing_the_run_between_sending_an_unmatched_alert_and_saving_it_sends_it_once`).
6. **Cleanup removes only staging, zip parts in the inbox and resolved review holds, 14 days after the fact.** Staging (`_inbox/<person>/export-<id>/`) and the export's zip parts go 14 days after the run finished, only for an `imported` export whose every pending review has a verified held copy (a regular file, not a link, in `_inbox/<person>/review/export-<id>/`, with the same SHA-1 as the staged item); that check is saved as a `cleanup_holds_verified` event, committed before any staging is removed, and the event records each pending hold's SHA-1, and once staging is gone a later run finishes the remaining zip parts only if that record exists and every pending hold is still a regular file with the recorded SHA-1 (without the record, or with any hold missing, a link or different, everything is kept); a review hold goes 14 days after its item was resolved and only when no pending or recently resolved item shares the file. Every removal goes through `paths.remove_inbox_tree`/`remove_inbox_file`, which refuse a link, anything outside `_inbox/<person>/`, and anything under or containing an `originals/` or `google-only/` folder; parts outside the photo folder are never removed. Held by `tests/test_cleanup.py` (negative tests for originals, google-only, pending holds that are missing, links, elsewhere or different (also after staging is gone), shared holds, links, tampered hold paths and parts redirected into originals or google-only). No Semgrep rule covers these removals: `darkroom-originals-read-only` sees only paths taken from `Photos.originals`/`original`/`uploads_tmp` or `originals_path`, and the removers live in `darkroom/storage/paths.py`, which it excludes.
7. **Cleanup never removes the only local copy of an item that failed to import, and a filesystem error never stops it silently.** While the latest finished run of an export has `failed > 0`, its staging and zip parts are kept (one `cleanup_kept` event says so, not repeated). An `OSError` while cleaning one export or hold records a `cleanup_failed` event with the error type only and cleanup goes on with the rest. Held by `tests/test_cleanup.py` (`test_a_run_with_items_that_could_not_be_imported_keeps_staging_and_parts`, `test_a_filesystem_error_is_recorded_and_the_rest_of_cleanup_goes_on`, `test_a_filesystem_error_on_a_hold_is_recorded_and_the_hold_kept`).
8. **The summary alert is sent at most once per export.** Its alert row (keyed `export_imported:<id>`, marked sent and closed at once so repeats never send it) is committed before it is sent, through `alerts.open_alert_committed`; a run killed after sending, or whose save after sending fails, is left to resume rather than marked failed, and the resumed run finds the row and does not send again. Held by `tests/test_import_run.py` (`CrashTests.test_killing_the_run_between_sending_the_summary_and_saving_it_sends_it_once`, `test_a_failed_save_after_the_summary_is_sent_leaves_the_run_to_resume_not_failed`).
